correction.critique: Strongest feature: Licona distinguishes companion participation from personal identification, grounding the former in first-person travel narration and presenting Luke as a probabilistic inference rather than certainty. Principal limitation: The identification remains dependent upon disputed external attribution, while the excerpt neither discriminates Luke from Pauline coworkers nor eliminates literary convention, source incorporation, or another companion. Live burden: The argument must demonstrate why autobiographical narration is historically preferable to compositional alternatives and why converging evidence specifically selects Luke instead of merely establishing an unidentified Pauline associate. Locked score: At 82, this strong, centrally relevant, unusually precise constructive earns considerable credit for its restrained conclusion and internal evidence, although underdetermination at the crucial identification step prevents a higher evidential-warrant assessment.
